title: Payer-Covered Items Are Not Billed to the Resident: Ancillary and Optional Services Billing Coverage Policy
content:
**Policy.** Under Ancillary and Optional Services Billing, what the resident's payer covers is never billed to the resident.

1. During a Part A stay, consolidated billing bundles covered supplies, drugs, lab and radiology into the per diem, so they are neither claimed separately nor charged to the resident; only the consolidated billing exclusions are billed by their own providers.
2. A Medicaid resident is never charged for anything the Medicaid per diem includes.
3. A hospice resident's drugs, supplies and equipment related to the terminal illness are the hospice's.
4. A Medicare Advantage item is supplied under the plan's authorization and the resident owes only the patient responsibility on the plan's remittance.
5. Durable medical equipment used in the center is not a Part B item.
6. Prescription drugs outside a Part A stay are billed by the contracted pharmacy, not the center.
7. An item is charged to the resident only when the resident's payer does not cover it.
8. A covered item is claimed to the payer within that payer's timely filing limit, and an item the center failed to claim in time is never shifted to the resident.

## Condition for a charge to the resident

An item is charged to the resident only when the resident's payer does not cover it. The judgement rests on the company's records, read before the charge is posted: the ancillary account the charge would be posted to, the tier that account is in, and the category of the item. The payer is the one the account's tier names, together with that tier's settings for consolidated billing, hospice coverage and Medicare Advantage authorization, and the product's lists of services outside consolidated billing, of items the Medicaid per diem includes, and its settings for durable medical equipment, pharmacy billing and the timely filing limits.

## Situations and treatment

| Situation | Treatment under this policy |
|---|---|
| Covered supply, drug, lab or radiology item during a Part A stay | Bundled into the per diem; not claimed separately; not charged to the resident |
| Consolidated billing exclusion during a Part A stay | Billed by its own provider |
| Item the Medicaid per diem includes, for a Medicaid resident | Never charged to the resident |
| Drug, supply or equipment related to a hospice resident's terminal illness | The hospice's |
| Medicare Advantage item | Supplied under the plan's authorization; the resident owes only the patient responsibility on the plan's remittance |
| Durable medical equipment used in the center | Not a Part B item |
| Prescription drug outside a Part A stay | Billed by the contracted pharmacy, not the center |
| Covered item | Claimed to the payer within that payer's timely filing limit |
| Covered item the center failed to claim in time | Never shifted to the resident |

## Questions answered by the policy

- **The resident's payer covers the item. May the resident be charged for it?** No. An item is charged to the resident only when the resident's payer does not cover it.
- **A covered item was not claimed within the payer's timely filing limit. Does the charge move to the resident?** No; an item the center failed to claim in time is never shifted to the resident.
- **What does a Medicare Advantage resident owe for a covered item?** Only the patient responsibility shown on the plan's remittance.
